title: Networked level transmitter not reachable
summary: After the level transmitter was replaced the tank no longer fills and the communication status is bad.
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1 (normally open). *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2 (normally closed). *)
    LevelHighHigh : BOOL; (* Independent high-high switch at 90 % (TRUE when wet). *)
    LevelPermille : INT; (* Level from Modbus holding register 0 (40001), 0..1000 = 0..100 %. *)
    LevelPercent : REAL; (* Level from holding registers 1-2 (40002-40003), IEEE 754 float, high word first. *)
    LevelCommOK : BOOL; (* TRUE while the Modbus scan of the transmitter succeeds. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    InletValve : BOOL; (* Inlet valve solenoid XV-101. *)
    DrainPump : BOOL; (* Drain pump P-102. *)
END_VAR
VAR
    Filling : BOOL;
END_VAR

Filling := (StartPB OR Filling) AND StopPB AND LevelCommOK AND NOT LevelHighHigh AND LevelPermille < 800;
InletValve := Filling;
DrainPump := FALSE;

END_PROGRAM
instructions: Run the simulation and check LevelCommOK and the Network tab.
Ping the documented transmitter address from the PLC.
Check the diagnostic buffer for connection errors.
hints: Read the connection status: is it a timeout, a refusal, an exception or no route?
A replacement device often arrives with a different default address.

criteria.title: The valve closes at 80 %
criteria.onFail: InletValve stayed open after the networked level reached 80 %.

criteria.title: Filling requires valid communication
criteria.onFail: The valve was open while the transmitter was not communicating.

troubleshooting.symptom: Since the transmitter was exchanged, the tank does not fill. The HMI shows 'level communication fault'.

diagnosisOptions.label: The Ethernet cable to the transmitter is broken
The new transmitter uses an IP address in another subnet
The PLC reads the wrong Modbus register
The Modbus unit identifier is wrong
The PLC Ethernet port is defective

repairs.label: Set the transmitter's IP address to the documented 192.168.0.20

debrief.rootCause: The replacement level transmitter kept an IP address in another subnet (192.168.1.20) instead of the documented 192.168.0.20. The PLC's Modbus client kept asking an address that no device answered.
evidence: LevelCommOK was FALSE and the client connection reported repeated timeouts.
A ping to the documented address 192.168.0.20 timed out: nothing on the network used that address.
A ping to 192.168.1.20 reported no route: the device existed, but in a subnet the PLC cannot reach without a gateway.
The fault started with the device exchange; the PLC program and its network settings were unchanged.
debrief.repair: Set the transmitter's IP address to the documented 192.168.0.20, then verify that the tank fills and the communication status stays OK.
debrief.reasoning: Classify the communication error first: a timeout, a refusal, an exception and no route each point to a different layer. A replacement device with a factory or old address is a frequent cause of timeouts after an exchange.
